items.title: Kenya records 100% Ebola contact tracing as surveillance remains heightened
items.description: Kenya has achieved 100% Ebola contact tracing coverage, surpassing the 85% global benchmark, with all 135 contacts successfully traced.
content: Kenya has achieved 100% Ebola contact tracing coverage, surpassing the 85% global benchmark, with all 135 contacts successfully traced.
No new cases have been reported since 19 October 2026, and there is no evidence of community transmission. The final batch of contacts was released on 11 November following completion of monitoring.

The country is on day six of the mandatory 42-day countdown towards an anticipated Ebola-free declaration on 23 December 2026, subject to no new confirmed cases. Surveillance, traveller screening and other response measures remain heightened.

Cabinet Secretary for Health Hon. Aden Duale highlighted the progress when he appeared before the Senate Standing Committee on Delegated Legislation, chaired by Tharaka Nithi Senator Hon. Mwenda Gataya, at Bunge Towers, Nairobi.

The Committee deliberated on the Public Health (Declaration of Formidable Epidemic Disease) Order, 2026 and the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026, published under Legal Notices No. 203 and 204.
The CS outlined the legal framework underpinning the response, including provisions for surveillance, testing, isolation, contact tracing, quarantine and infection prevention.
He explained that the urgency of the outbreak necessitated the instruments’ publication without prior public participation, in accordance with Section 5A(2) of the Statutory Instruments Act.

More than 810,000 travellers have been screened across 26 points of entry, with nearly 5,000 response personnel on standby, over 4,900 trained healthcare workers, 349 rapid response teams and five designated testing laboratories supporting preparedness.
The CS called for continued implementation of the regulations to strengthen public health protection and response coordination.
He was accompanied by PS Mary Muthoni, DG Health Dr Patrick Amoth, Acting KNPHI DG Dr Maureen Kamene, Director of Public Health Dr Stephen Muleshe and other Ministry officials.

Court overturns Sh4m award to former police officer sacked over suspicious M-Pesa transactions
items.description: The former senior police officer was dismissed in 2016.
content: Vigilance House in Nairobi, the National Police Service headquarters. Court of Appeal has overturned a Sh4 million compensation awarded to a former senior police officer dismissed in 2016.

The Court of Appeal has overturned a Sh4 million compensation awarded to a former senior police officer who was dismissed in 2016 after failing a vetting exercise conducted by the National Police Service Commission (NPSC).

A three-judge bench ruled that Peter Kilonzo Katheka, a former Chief Inspector of Police, was accorded a fair hearing and given an opportunity to explain suspicious M-Pesa transactions that formed the basis of the decision to remove him from the service.
The judges said the transactions, which the Commission considered inconsistent with his declared income, were presented to him during the vetting process, and he was allowed to explain their source.

Katheka, who joined the police service in 1984, told the panel that some of the transactions involved welfare contributions and private business dealings. During a subsequent review, he explained his dealings with a businessman identified as Sammy as loan repayments.
However, the Commission was not satisfied with his explanations and declared him unsuitable for continued service.
“The 1st respondent’s record was before the panel and was considered. We are not persuaded that his removal was disproportionate to the concern established,” the judges ruled.

The former officer had challenged the legality and fairness of the vetting process, arguing that the Commission relied on adverse information that had not been disclosed to him and failed to give adequate reasons for its decision.
He also complained that his long service record was disregarded, the hearing was hostile and the panel was irregularly constituted.

The Employment and Labour Relations Court (ELRC) upheld the Commission's conduct of the vetting but, on its own motion, declared Regulation 13 of the National Police Service (Vetting) Regulations, 2013 unconstitutional. It subsequently awarded Katheka Sh4 million for violation of his constitutional rights.
The Commission challenged the decision, arguing that the judge had improperly invalidated the regulation without inviting the parties to address its constitutionality.
Also Read: Fake degree, real salary - EACC wants Sh40.3m back from former KeRRA boss
The Court of Appeal agreed, saying the petition had not challenged the validity of Regulation 13 and none of the parties had made submissions on the question.
A customer withdraws money from an M-Pesa shop. Suspicious M-Pesa transactions formed the basis of the decision to remove the former senior police officer from the service.
It faulted the trial judge for introducing the constitutional issue on his own and making it the foundation of the relief granted.
“The gravity of a constitutional question is no licence to determine it in disregard of the very procedural fairness the Constitution guarantees,” the judges said.

The appellate court clarified that its decision did not determine whether Regulation 13 was constitutionally valid, noting that the question would have to be considered in a case where it was properly pleaded and argued.
On the fairness of the vetting exercise, the judges said the Commission's mandate to assess the suitability and integrity of police officers served a legitimate public interest.

They noted that vetting was not a criminal trial and did not automatically attract all the protections under Article 50(2) of the Constitution. However, its administrative nature did not exempt the Commission from complying with Article 47 on fair administrative action.
Also Read: Fake papers that get real jobs: Inside Kenya’s public service fraud

“We therefore agree with the Commission that vetting is not a criminal trial, and that Article 50(2) is not engaged wholesale merely because the inquiry touches on potentially improper transactions. The converse is equally true: labelling a process administrative does not strip it of the protections of a fair hearing,” the court said.

The judges observed that Katheka appeared before the vetting panel on August 23, 2016, and later sought a review after the Commission declared him unsuitable in a decision communicated to him in December that year.
The review was heard in July 2017 but dismissed the following month.

The Commission maintained that his frequent and substantial M-Pesa transactions with fellow officers and civilians could not be reconciled with his declared earnings, and that his explanations were not supported by the accounts of the people involved.
The former officer, however, argued that he had served for 33 years without blemish and that the Commission's findings were based on conjecture rather than sufficient evidence.
He also maintained that denying him compensation after losing his income, benefits and career prospects would leave him without an effective remedy.
The appellate judges rejected that argument, holding that financial loss could only inform the remedy after a violation of rights had been established.

“His loss of income, benefits and prospects may inform the remedy once liability is established; it cannot establish liability. Nor does the unavailability of reinstatement found an entitlement to constitutional damages,” they said.

Kenyans pursuing postgraduate education abroad have seven fully funded scholarship opportunities closing between November 30 and December 1, 2026, covering programmes in China, Switzerland, Singapore, the United Kingdom and Hong Kong.
The awards target master's and doctoral students across a broad range of disciplines, with funding packages that in some cases cover tuition, accommodation, stipends, travel and research expenses.

The Yenching Academy of Peking University is accepting applications for its two-year master's programme in China studies until November 30, 2026, at 9am Beijing time.
Open to international graduates with a bachelor's degree in any field, the fellowship includes tuition, university accommodation, a monthly stipend and one return air ticket.
English proficiency is required, though graduates of English-taught programmes may qualify for an exemption.
Also closing on November 30 is the ETH Zurich Excellence Scholarship and Opportunity Programme (ESOP), which supports outstanding students pursuing master's degrees at the Swiss institution.
From the 2027/28 academic year, the award provides a tuition fee waiver and CHF 13,500 per semester, alongside mentorship and access to the ETH Foundation network.
Applicants must generally rank in the top 10% of their bachelor's class and submit a research proposal for their master's thesis. The deadline is 11:59am Central European Time.

The Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships also close on November 30, targeting early-career researchers who have completed a master's degree and wish to pursue research or doctoral studies at Swiss universities.
Successful research scholarship recipients receive a monthly allowance of approximately CHF 2,450. Applicants must secure the backing of an academic supervisor in Switzerland before applying.
The Graduate Ellison Scholars Programme offers fully funded doctoral places at the University of Oxford for the October 2027 intake.
Supported by the Ellison Institute of Technology, the programme funds research in artificial intelligence, engineering, economics, biology, plant sciences, chemistry and mathematics.
The package covers tuition, a living stipend, travel, conference participation, technology and arrival costs. The application deadline is December 1, 2026, at 5pm UK time.
The Hong Kong Research Grants Council is offering 400 fellowships through its Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme for the 2027/28 academic year.

Each scholar receives an annual stipend of HK$344,400 and a yearly travel allowance of HK$14,400 for up to three years.
Applications close at noon Hong Kong time on December 1.
The University of Hong Kong's Presidential PhD Scholarship , also closing December 1, is open to outstanding international doctoral applicants.
The package is valued at up to HK$445,800 in the first year and includes a monthly postgraduate scholarship of HK$28,700, a tuition waiver, a cash award and a guaranteed hall place.
Applicants to full-time PhD programmes at HKU are automatically considered for the award.

Finally, the Singapore International Graduate Award (SINGA) supports doctoral research in science and engineering at leading Singaporean universities and research institutions, including those affiliated with A*STAR, the National University of Singapore and Nanyang Technological University.
The package includes full tuition, a monthly stipend of S$2,700 rising to S$3,200 after the qualifying examination, a one-time airfare grant and a settling-in allowance.

The December 1 date is the published recurring deadline for the August intake; applicants should confirm the 2027 intake deadline directly with A*STAR before submitting.

Prospective applicants are advised to prepare academic transcripts, recommendation letters and research proposals well ahead of the deadlines, as all awards are competitive and meeting minimum requirements does not guarantee selection.

Some deadlines arrive as early as November 2026, and the fully funded awards can cover tuition, accommodation, living costs and travel.
Applicants must apply through the universities, not the Foundation, and should prepare their documents promptly.

The High Commission of Canada in Kenya has opened applications for a Trade Programme Coordinator, offering a gross annual salary of KSh 3,078,605 plus benefits on a full-time, indeterminate contract.

The position, classified as LE-A3 under the Locally Engaged Staff (LES) framework, is based at the High Commission in Nairobi. Only one vacancy is available, and the application window closes on November 18, 2026, at 23:59 local time.
The selection process is open to all individuals residing in Kenya who hold valid authorisation to work in the country.

Candidates must hold a bachelor's degree from a recognised university and demonstrate advanced proficiency in English across reading, writing, comprehension, and speaking.
A minimum of three years of recent administrative support experience, gained within the last five years, is required, covering areas such as organising meetings, events, and stakeholder engagements.
At least two years of experience conducting research and building relationships with clients or partners is also mandatory.

Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite is essential, alongside knowledge of Kenyan political, economic, and business environments. The role demands strong judgement, organisational ability, and the capacity to work with diverse teams.

The Government of Canada states it does not negotiate salaries and that remuneration is determined by an established multi-step pay scale aligned with local labour conditions in Kenya.
Competitive benefits consistent with local practices are included in the total compensation package.

Waiguru asks Mt. Kenya not to undermine its interests by abandoning Ruto
items.description: Kirinyaga Governor Anne Waiguru has defended her decision to support the re-election of President William Ruto, saying abandoning the government could leave Mt. Kenya without representation at the national decision-making table.
content: Waiguru said the 2027 political numbers favour President Ruto’s re-election and that Mt. Kenya would be disadvantaged if it had no representation in the national decision-making structure.

Speaking during a women empowerment event in Githunguri, Kiambu County, Waiguru asked voters in the region to remain firmly in government, warning against making political decisions that could undermine their interests.
She argued that abandoning the government would be counterproductive, particularly when the region has an opportunity to remain part of the national leadership and decision-making structure.

The Governor, who has declared her bid for the Deputy President position, also cautioned the region against voting for the opposition in 2027 in protest over the fallout between President Ruto and former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua.

“Abandoning this government that you put in place for the opposition would be like cutting your nose to spite your mouth. Let not be dragged into personal differences between individuals, we must put our interest first,” she said.
Waiguru asked voters to rally behind leaders based on their development track records and ability to deliver rather than political party affiliations.

“We have decided to stay with William Ruto, his work speaks for itself, from roads to markets and affordable housing. He is working, and the noise from the opposition will not change this. We are not going to vote for political parties; we will vote for leaders of substance,” she said.
She said the Mt. Kenya region should not take for granted the progress it had made by virtue of being in government.
She called for greater representation of women in national leadership, saying this was necessary to address some of the challenges facing the people.

Waiguru said challenges facing women could only be adequately addressed if they were represented in decision-making positions, adding that she was ready to take on greater national leadership responsibilities.

The Governor said her experience in leadership, including serving as Cabinet Secretary, Governor and Chairperson of the Council of Governors (CoG), had given her a broader understanding of the challenges facing the country and the need for women’s inclusion in top leadership.

“I have served as the Chairperson of the Council of Governors and was re-elected unopposed. I have travelled across the country and understand our politics. Having looked at the situation, I have come to the conclusion that many of the challenges women face stem from the absence of women at the decision-making table,” she said.
She said every Kenyan had a democratic right to seek elective leadership positions and that people should be allowed to pursue their political ambitions without hostility.
“Competition for political leadership is a normal feature of democracy and every five years those aspiring for positions must be prepared to engage voters and seek their support,” she added.
Her position was backed by Kiambu Woman Representative Anne Wamuratha, who asked women to support Waiguru’s bid for national leadership, citing her track record.
“Women must be at the table when national matters are being discussed, and Waiguru is fit for the Deputy President position,” Wamuratha said.
Wamuratha urged Mt. Kenya residents to maintain their support for President Ruto, warning that antagonising the government could undermine the region’s access to development opportunities.

The MP urged Kiambu residents to safeguard their political influence, noting that the county commands more than one million votes and should not allow itself to be used as a bargaining chip in the political interests of individual leaders.

“We voted for him, and we have to stay in government and get the development that is owed to us. If we, as the people of Mt Kenya, keep antagonizing him, he will take development elsewhere. Let us be wise and not just join others in hating Ruto when he has delivered,” she said.
Kirinyaga Central MP Gachoki Gitari also backed Waiguru’s national leadership ambitions, saying her development record in Kirinyaga demonstrated her capacity to serve at the national level.

“Governor Anne Waiguru has delivered for the people of Kirinyaga, and now we are looking forward to seeing her at the national table. We are proponents of Usawa ni Sawa, including in matters of gender, and we believe Waiguru is fit and ready for the Deputy President position,” he said.

items.description: A Uasin Gishu procurement officer has been charged with allegedly obtaining KSh 115,000 from a police officer by promising to secure his promotion.

A Uasin Gishu County Government employee has been charged with allegedly defrauding a police officer of KSh 115,000 after promising to facilitate his promotion to the rank of sergeant.

The suspect, identified as Daniel Kemboi Kuyo, 40, works as a procurement officer at the county government and is accused of impersonating a Human Resource officer attached to the National Police Service Commission (NPSC).

Kuyo was arrested in the Outspan area of Kapseret following an intelligence-led operation conducted by detectives from the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI).

He was subsequently taken to Eldoret Central Police Station for processing before being presented at the Eldoret Law Courts.
Appearing before Senior Resident Magistrate Keyne Gweno, Kuyo denied a charge of cheating contrary to Section 315 of the Penal Code.
The prosecution alleged that he obtained KSh 115,000 from police officer Stanley Kogo by falsely claiming that he could secure his promotion to the rank of sergeant.
According to the charge, Kuyo allegedly committed the offence on diverse dates between September 21 and November 3, 2026, in the Outspan area of Kapseret Sub-County, Uasin Gishu County.
During the court proceedings, the accused asked the magistrate to grant him lenient bond and cash bail terms, arguing that he was not a flight risk.
Magistrate Gweno ordered his release on a bond of KSh 200,000 with one surety of a similar amount. Alternatively, he was granted a cash bail option of KSh 150,000.
The case will be mentioned on November 30, 2026, for further directions.

Esri Eastern Africa Appoints Faith Nkatha Gitonga As CEO
items.description: Esri Eastern Africa has appointed Faith Nkatha Gitonga, who most recently worked at the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change (TBI), as its new CEO
content: Esri Eastern Africa has appointed Faith Nkatha Gitonga, a technology and digital transformation leader who most recently worked at the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change (TBI), as its new Chief Executive Officer. She takes over leadership of the regional business on December 1, 2026.

Gitonga joins from TBI, where she served as interim Kenya country director and head of technology and digital transformation for Africa Advisory until April 2026. In that role, she worked on technology-driven reform in the public sector, experience that is directly relevant as governments across the region turn to geospatial intelligence, location analytics and digital mapping to plan infrastructure, manage resources, deliver services and make strategic decisions.

Before TBI, Gitonga led Cellulant’s Kenyan operations as country manager from 2020 to 2023, running one of the country’s prominent fintech businesses. Earlier in her career, she headed Oracle’s digital transformation business for Kenya’s public sector and held senior strategy and banking roles at Sidian Bank and Chase Bank. In all, she brings more than 15 years of leadership experience across financial services, payments, technology and public-sector transformation.
She also brings governance experience from the boards of Capital A Investment Bank, TechnoServe, PAL Network and LVCT Health, spanning business, development and corporate governance.

Esri Eastern Africa distributes geographic information systems (GIS) technology, including the ArcGIS platform, alongside spatial analytics, mapping, consulting and training services. Headquartered in Nairobi, it serves customers in Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania and Ethiopia.

items.title: Jinko Solar hosts Jinko Academy in Kenya to build local solar expertise
items.description: Jinko Solar held the Jinko Academy in Kenya with Jomo Kenyatta University of Agriculture and Technology (JKUAT) and the University of Nairobi. The
content: Jinko Solar, a global leader in photovoltaic technology and Battery Energy Storage Systems, has hosted the Jinko Academy in Kenya, bringing together academia and industry to strengthen local technical expertise in solar energy. The programme was delivered in collaboration with two of the country’s leading institutions, JKUAT and the University of Nairobi.

The Jinko Academy is designed to close the gap between theoretical learning and practical application in the renewable energy sector. Through its partnership with the two universities, Jinko Solar aims to equip students, researchers and local engineers with the skills needed to support Kenya’s growing solar industry and its Vision 2030 renewable energy goals.

The initiative comes at an important moment for Kenya’s energy landscape. Jinko Solar has a well established presence in the region. It supplied modules for the 50 MW Garissa solar plant and remains a leading module exporter to the Kenyan market. More recently, the company supplied its Tiger Neo 3.0 modules for Kenya’s largest private healthcare solar project, which covers more than 780 private hospitals nationwide.

During the academy sessions, participants worked directly with Jinko Solar’s technical experts on module manufacturing, system design and smart grid operations. The training also stressed practical applications, particularly in the high temperature and high irradiance conditions typical of Kenya, where reliable performance is critical.

The Jinko Academy reflects the company’s wider commitment to building capacity in emerging markets. As Kenya pursues an ambitious renewable energy agenda, partnerships between global technology leaders and local academic institutions are seen as essential to creating a skilled, self reliant workforce able to maintain and expand the country’s solar infrastructure.

Kenya records 100% Ebola contact tracing as surveillance remains heightened
items.description: Kenya has achieved 100% Ebola contact tracing coverage, surpassing the 85% global benchmark, with all 135 contacts successfully traced.
content: Kenya has achieved 100% Ebola contact tracing coverage, surpassing the 85% global benchmark, with all 135 contacts successfully traced.
No new cases have been reported since 19 October 2026, and there is no evidence of community transmission. The final batch of contacts was released on 11 November following completion of monitoring.

The country is on day six of the mandatory 42-day countdown towards an anticipated Ebola-free declaration on 23 December 2026, subject to no new confirmed cases. Surveillance, traveller screening and other response measures remain heightened.

Cabinet Secretary for Health Hon. Aden Duale highlighted the progress when he appeared before the Senate Standing Committee on Delegated Legislation, chaired by Tharaka Nithi Senator Hon. Mwenda Gataya, at Bunge Towers, Nairobi.

The Committee deliberated on the Public Health (Declaration of Formidable Epidemic Disease) Order, 2026 and the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026, published under Legal Notices No. 203 and 204.
The CS outlined the legal framework underpinning the response, including provisions for surveillance, testing, isolation, contact tracing, quarantine and infection prevention.
He explained that the urgency of the outbreak necessitated the instruments’ publication without prior public participation, in accordance with Section 5A(2) of the Statutory Instruments Act.

More than 810,000 travellers have been screened across 26 points of entry, with nearly 5,000 response personnel on standby, over 4,900 trained healthcare workers, 349 rapid response teams and five designated testing laboratories supporting preparedness.
The CS called for continued implementation of the regulations to strengthen public health protection and response coordination.
He was accompanied by PS Mary Muthoni, DG Health Dr Patrick Amoth, Acting KNPHI DG Dr Maureen Kamene, Director of Public Health Dr Stephen Muleshe and other Ministry officials.

The hidden cost of living with diabetes in Kenya
items.description: By Lenah Bosibori Erick Omondi has lived with Type 1 diabetes for 23 years. He was diagnosed at the age of 17, after his parents repeatedly dismissed the symptoms, he had been experiencing. When he joined Form One, he began documenting the symptoms, hoping to understand what was happening to his body. His condition eventually […]
content: Erick Omondi has lived with Type 1 diabetes for 23 years. He was diagnosed at the age of 17, after his parents repeatedly dismissed the symptoms, he had been experiencing.
When he joined Form One, he began documenting the symptoms, hoping to understand what was happening to his body. His condition eventually led him to hospital, where he was diagnosed with diabetes.

“When I used to eat a lot and drink a lot of water, my parents thought it was normal. Since we were many people in the house, they assumed I was eating more because there was little food to go around. They did not recognize these as signs of Type 1 diabetes,” said Omondi during the World Diabetes Day commemoration at Mbagathi Hospital.

For people living with diabetes, getting a diagnosis is only the beginning of a lifelong journey. Keeping the condition under control means taking medication regularly, attending clinic appointments and making changes to their diet. But these are not always easy when money is limited.
Omondi has to inject himself with insulin four times a day. He also carries sweets in his bag to help raise his blood sugar whenever it drops.

Caroline Moraa is another patient who has been living with Type 2 diabetes for the past three years. She says the cost of medication remains a recurring challenge. At times, she has to buy her medicine out of pocket, and when she cannot afford it, accessing the treatment she needs becomes difficult

“Sometimes I go and find that I don’t have the medicine. I have to buy it, but if I don’t have money, it becomes difficult,” she said, explaining that some of the medicines cost between Sh500 and Sh600.

Her experience reflects some of the challenges facing people living with diabetes in Kenya, where access to screening and treatment remains a concern, particularly for those from low-income households.
At Mbagathi Hospital in Nairobi, health workers and partners are trying to make diabetes services more accessible through an expanded clinic that now operates five days a week.
The facility marked World Diabetes Day by calling for greater awareness, early diagnosis and improved access to care, under the theme of early action on diabetes.
Jacob Mollerup, General Manager of Novo Nordisk Middle Africa, said the clinic had increased its capacity to serve patients since opening two months earlier.
“Before, they used to see people with diabetes once or twice every week. Now they can see them five times a week,” he said.
He said the expansion had reduced waiting times and created more opportunities for people to get screened, tested and receive follow-up care.
Mollerup urged people to take advantage of the services, noting that many residents were still unaware that the clinic had expanded its operating days.
According to the International Diabetes Federation, an estimated 800,000 people are living with diabetes in Kenya. Mollerup said about 400,000 of them were unaware of their condition.

“That’s a call to action to come to a place like Mbagathi or any other hospital, get screened, get tested and get some advice. If you have diabetes, you can get good care and begin your journey,” he said.

Dr Ericah Koima, the Medical Superintendent at Mbagathi Hospital, said the facility had registered more than 2,000 people living with diabetes and attends to an average of 250 to 300 patients every month.

She said patients previously received diabetes services only twice a week, but the expanded clinic now operates from Monday to Friday, including attending to patients who walk in without appointments.
The facility has specialists attending to patients daily, alongside testing, medication and health education services.
“Some come when they are very sick. But with the quality of care they receive here, we have specialists attending to them. We have seen our patients improve and their lives improve,” she said.
However, access to treatment remains a challenge for some patients, particularly those who struggle to afford medicines.

Koima said the hospital had previously experienced difficulties supplying insulin to people with Type 1 diabetes. However, with support from the Ministry of Health and partners, it was now providing insulin free of charge to patients under the age of 25.
She also encouraged patients to keep their appointments and follow medical advice rather than abandon prescribed treatment for herbal remedies.
Dr Moses Owino, Nairobi City County’s Director of Medical Services, said diabetes is among the non-communicable diseases requiring stronger public health attention.

He said the condition could lead to serious complications, including stroke, kidney failure and heart disease, when blood sugar levels are not properly managed. Managing diabetes involves medication, health education and lifestyle changes, including regular physical activity and a balanced diet.

Dr Owino said screening is also important because some people may not recognize the symptoms of diabetes until the condition have progressed. “Common warning signs include excessive thirst, increased hunger, unexplained weight loss and frequent urination, including waking up several times at night to use the bathroom,” said Dr Owino

Nairobi has 119 functional hospitals, according to Owino, with several public facilities offering diabetes screening, laboratory tests, specialist care and medication. He adds that the county is also working to strengthen services at lower-level facilities so that patients could receive care closer to where they live rather than travelling to major hospitals.
“Community Health Promoters are expected to support these efforts by helping identify people who may need screening and directing them to health facilities,” Dr Owino said.
But expanding services is only part of the challenge. Patients must also be able to access the medicines and follow-up are they need over the long term.

Owino said the county is working to improve infrastructure, equipment, medicine supplies and the availability of health workers across its facilities. He also encouraged patients who encounter medicine shortages to report them through the county’s toll-free number, 1508.
Mollerup said Novo Nordisk has been working with the Ministry of Health, county governments and other partners to improve diabetes care in Kenya.
He said the company has supported the establishment of 92 centres for driving change across the country, working with public health institutions to strengthen the quality of care.

The company, which has been involved in diabetes treatment for more than a century, has also introduced newer medicines in Kenya while continuing to supply insulin used by people living with diabetes.

He also highlighted the different uses of some of the medicines available. Ozempic is approved for Type 2 diabetes, while Wegovy is approved for weight management in people living with obesity, he explained.
As Kenya marks World Diabetes Day, health workers say early diagnosis, regular treatment and lifestyle changes remain central to managing the condition.
